assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling made aryl amines routinely accessible and is used across pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and organic electronic materials. Original, clearly defined, and lasting; a classic enabling method of the kind I value.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general, ligand-controlled catalytic systems that made the reaction broadly usable. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor but not the general method, so a two-person prize is the cleanest configuration.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent confirmation and industrial use; the field is stable and recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Treatment of the Kosugi precedent and the relation to the 2010 cross-coupling prize may be debated.
I rely on my own recollection of the discovery timeline and have not verified it independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mesoporous nanocrystalline TiO2 sensitized with molecular dyes gave an efficient photoelectrochemical cell, a designed architecture whose structure sets function. It opened a field of molecular photovoltaics and led on to perovskite cells.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 Nature paper by O'Regan and Grätzel is the defining contribution. Hagfeldt is credited for later mechanistic and device development, which I regard as a secondary contribution.
assessment.maturity: More than thirty years of work, with certified efficiencies and commercial niches. Its practical impact is smaller than first predicted, but the scientific impact is clear.
uncertainties: Real-world impact is modest compared with silicon photovoltaics.
Whether to credit O'Regan alongside Grätzel is a committee judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers produced a rapid, extraordinary rise in solar-cell efficiency and a new class of defect-tolerant semiconductors. This is a materials-structure-function story of great breadth.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitized cell, Park made the first solid-state cell, and Snaith made the efficient mesostructured and planar devices. Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel also made significant contributions, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency and the basic physics are well confirmed by many groups. Long-term operational stability and lead toxicity remain unresolved, so it may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Stability and commercial viability are unproven.
Priority and credit among the many contributors are contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at XFELs gave structures from micro- and nanocrystals with radiation damage outrun, and enabled time-resolved structural studies. As an enabling method for crystals too small for conventional X-ray diffraction, it is close to my own field.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the proof-of-principle work and the method development. Fromme and Schlichting made decisive biological and time-resolved applications. Hajdu and others also contributed; I am not certain of the full early-credit picture.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across several facilities, with growing time-resolved results. The key scientific results are maturing but not all are fully established.
uncertainties: Dependence on a few large facilities limits the breadth of use.
Overlap with microED and 3D ED methods and allocation among many contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silicas (M41S/MCM-41, SBA-15 and related) opened pore sizes beyond zeolites and created a lasting platform for catalysts, adsorbents and supports. It is a rational design concept grounded in structure.
assessment.attribution: The Mobil team (Kresge, Beck and colleagues) made the discovery. Ryoo and Stucky/Zhao did the key follow-on work on ordered carbons and large-pore silicas. Inagaki's FSM-16 is an independent route with a contested priority claim. Allocation is difficult.
assessment.maturity: A mature field with thousands of applications, though the leading industrial applications have been modest, and the recognition has been delayed.
uncertainties: Priority between the Mobil and Japanese (FSM-16) work.
Whether the impact is Nobel-level or incremental after zeolites.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis created new reactivity for radical and polar bond formation and is widely adopted in synthesis and in pharmaceutical discovery.
assessment.attribution: MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson reported the three independent seminal 2008-2009 demonstrations. Earlier and parallel work by others (Fukuzumi, Kellogg, König, Nicewicz, Melchiorre) complicates the credit. MacMillan already shared the 2021 prize for organocatalysis.
assessment.maturity: Broad independent confirmation, and the method is now routine. The mechanistic details are still evolving.
uncertainties: A second prize for MacMillan is a difficult step.
Overlap with earlier photochemistry and attribution among many groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Designed molecular-sieve catalysts and zeolites with controlled pore architecture and active sites underpin refining and petrochemicals and emissions control. Structure determination and templating strategies have been central, and the area is close to my own expertise.
assessment.attribution: Davis, Corma and Zones are credited with major design and synthesis contributions to new frameworks and catalysts, but credit is spread widely across the field. Industrial and academic roles are hard to separate.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with strong industrial confirmation. The broad subject is diffuse and may lack a single clearly defined discovery.
uncertainties: No single discovery is clearly defined.
I have a possible conflict of interest because of my own research area.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR and relaxation methods enabled structure and dynamics determination of large proteins in solution, an enabling technology for structural biology, though Wüthrich's 2002 prize covers the foundations.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Kay and Clore made the decisive heteronuclear and isotope-labeling developments for larger systems. Palmer and Wagner also contributed substantially to relaxation methods and structure, and credit is shared among a larger community.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with widespread confirmation over decades.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier 2002 NMR recognition.
Allocation among more than three strong contributors.
